Perturbation probes have evidence as robustness diagnostics, but the retrieved studies do not establish that their scores predict which intervention improves held-out HR@10. [Oh et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12686) found that tiny training-data changes can substantially alter recommendations, with low-accuracy users more affected. [Betello et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13165) found strong sensitivity to removing recent interactions. These findings motivate position-aware probes; they do not establish that greater invariance is always desirable, because recent interactions can contain useful predictive information. Distinguish inference-time history perturbations from training-data perturbations requiring retraining.

Fixed sampled negatives make comparisons reproducible but do not establish full-catalog validity. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. Separately, [Dwork et al.](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2015/hash/bad5f33780c42f2588878a9d07405083-Abstract.html) show that adaptive holdout reuse can induce overfitting. Thus, repeated optimization against the pinned users and candidates risks selection bias; fixing candidates does not eliminate it. Preserve the required evaluator and interpret its score as the specified sampled-ranking objective.

Recommended priority: a small, preregistered falsification experiment before substantial diagnostic development. Keep official splits unchanged; measure probes on training histories and compare a few predefined interventions against SASRec using identical seeds and evaluation candidates. Before observing validation results, record each probe’s predicted improvement direction. Test whether those predictions explain paired HR@10 changes across all four categories beyond training loss and simple recency/popularity diagnostics. Report category results and paired user-bootstrap uncertainty; these intervals do not correct adaptive selection. Cap benchmark queries, reuse existing checkpoints, and drop probes that provide no incremental predictive value.
